newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Elektrowatt details profits, sale plans.
newsitem.headline: Elektrowatt details profits, sale plans.

text.p: Elektrowatt AG, the Swiss energy and industrial concern, said that its group net income from ongoing operations in the first half of its business year rose 40 percent to 143 million Swiss francs.
Consolidated revenues for the period, from October 1, 1996 to March 31, 1997 were 3.714 billion francs, up nine percent.
It also said it expected the trend in the second half of the year "to be much the same as that in the first six months."
It also said that a planned sale of most of a 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt now held by Credit Suisse was not likely to be completed before the end of 1997 or the beginning of 1998.
The industrial activities of Elektrowatt will be sold to Siemens AG .
The remainder of Elektrowatt, consisting of its energy activities, will be placed in a consortium called Watt AG. Owners comprise Swiss and German energy concerns.
Credit Suisse will keep a 20 percent stake in Watt.
"In the view of the Elektrowatt management, the final conclusion of these procedures is not now to be expected before the end of 1997 or the beginning of 1998," it said.
The following steps remains to be finalised before the sale can be completed, Elektrowatt said:
-- approval of U.S., Brussels and Swiss anti-trust authorities.
-- deliberations concerning Swiss real estate holdings.
-- a formal public takeover offer by CS.
-- an extraordinary shareholders' meeting to approve the spin-off.
-- allocation of Elektrowatt shares to Siemens and the Watt consortium.
